presentation_summary: 72-year-old woman had insidious lower back pain and stiffness that progressed to shoulder girdle symptoms with weight loss, fever, and malaise.
She was seen repeatedly for severe headache and had a normal CT brain.

Before rheumatology consultation, shoulder and hip girdle symptoms largely resolved without intervention, followed by severe right unilateral frontal and temporal headache and right upper-limb claudication.
Exam found reduced shoulder active range of motion, no temporal or axillary tenderness, palpable left temporal pulse but absent right temporal pulse, and normal radial/ulnar pulses.

CRP was 16 mg/L, ESR 17 mm/h, full blood count was normal except mild thrombocytosis, renal and liver function were normal; temporal ultrasound later showed right temporal artery halo/intima-media thickness.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Temporal artery ultrasound compatible with temporal arteritis

confirmatory_findings.finding: Rapid symptom improvement after high-dose oral prednisolone
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: started on high-dose oral prednisolone 60 mg daily, with rapid improvement in her symptoms

quality_warnings: Temporal ultrasound halo/intima-media thickness is stored only in confirmatory_findings.
